data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 5 files (.gitignore, .SRCINFO, LICENSE, .nvchecker.toml, PKGBUILD) and found them all safe. The PKGBUILD uses a pinned SHA-256 checksum for the source tarball from the project's own GitHub repository, standard CMake build workflows, and no suspicious commands. The qwen model's 'inconclusive' result was due to API errors (HTTP 400) preventing it from reviewing 3 files, not due to actual security concerns. The files it did review (.gitignore, PKGBUILD) were also found safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool execution failures, not substantive security analysis differences. The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 errors when attempting to audit .nvchecker.toml, .SRCINFO, and LICENSE, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found no issues. Both models agreed on the files they could review.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .nvchecker.toml, .SRCINFO, and LICENSE due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: API errors and tool failures should not be treated as security findings or contribute to an inconclusive verdict when another model successfully reviews the same files
When multiple models are used, a model with complete coverage that finds no issues should override a model with partial coverage due to tool errors

The audit system should distinguish between 'could not review due to tool error' and 'reviewed and found suspicious' - the former should not block a safe verdict if other models provide complete coverage
